questions.subject: Firebase
questions.question: Explain the difference between Firestore triggers and callable functions in Firebase.
questions.ideal_answer: Firestore triggers and callable functions differ in several ways: Firestore triggers is database event functions (works by reacting to document changes) whereas callable functions is client-callable HTTPS functions (works by authenticated client invocation). Firestore triggers is typically used for onCreate, onUpdate, onDelete, onWrite, while callable functions is used for automatic auth context, CORS handled. Example demonstrating Firestore triggers: functions.firestore.document('users/{userId}').onCreate((snap, context) => { ... }). Example demonstrating callable functions: const addMessage = httpsCallable(functions, 'addMessage'); const result = await addMessage({ text: 'Hello' });.

questions.subject: Firebase
questions.question: Explain the difference between queries and transactions in Firebase.
questions.ideal_answer: queries and transactions differ in several ways: queries is document retrieval (works by single-collection queries with indexing) whereas transactions is atomic multi-document operations (works by all-or-nothing updates). queries is typically used for where, orderBy, limit, startAfter, while transactions is used for read before write within transaction. Example demonstrating queries: db.collection('users').where('age', '>=', 18).orderBy('age').limit(10). Example demonstrating transactions: db.runTransaction(async (t) => { const doc = await t.get(ref); t.update(ref, { count: doc.data().count + 1 }); }).
follow_up_questions: Under what specific circumstances would you choose queries over transactions?
What is the performance or memory difference between queries and transactions?
